- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or neutral, model often overpredicts; reduce forecast to reflect bearish or stagnant sentiment.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >85), model frequently overshoots in the next 5–10 days; cap forecast at +5–10% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns neutral.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias in early 30d forecasts — if recent 5–7 day average is high, forecast should not rise further unless sentiment confirms breakout.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values (no sentiment), model tends to ignore volatility; in such cases, add 1–3% volatility buffer to forecast.
- For 30d horizon, model often underestimates late-period (last 10–15 days) price action — especially if sentiment turns positive mid-horizon; adjust forecast upward by 2–5% in final 10 days if sentiment >0.67.
- If sentiment history includes multiple 0.00 values followed by a 1.00, model may misread momentum; treat as “recovery” signal and increase forecast by 3–5% in next 5 days.
